intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that early-onset dystonia and/or spastic paraplegia (DYTSPG) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the ATP5MC3 gene (602736) on chromosome 2q31.

paragraphs.text: Early-onset dystonia and/or spastic paraplegia is an autosomal dominant neurologic disorder with variable presentation. Neilson et al. (2022) described it in a large family as childhood-onset, progressive generalized dystonia or adult-onset, gradually progressive spastic paraplegia. Less severe, later-onset focal limb and neck dystonia and spasmodic dysphonia also occurred. Zech et al. (2022) reported additional patients with pyramidal signs, spasticity, and developmental delay.

paragraphs.text: Gilbert et al. (2009) reported a large multigenerational Ohio kindred with a highly penetrant autosomal dominant neurologic disorder that caused spasticity and dystonia. Spasticity and weakness began anywhere from the first year of life to the sixth decade. Dystonia began between the first and third decades. Affected members had no ataxia and no apparent cognitive involvement. Neuroimaging and peripheral neurophysiology were normal.

paragraphs.text: Neilson et al. (2022) summarized a large multigenerational family (Family-1) segregating autosomal dominant dystonia and/or spastic paraplegia. Of 40 individuals in the pedigree, 18 were affected, with either childhood-onset, progressive generalized dystonia or adult-onset, gradually progressive spastic paraplegia. Less severe, later-onset focal limb and neck dystonia and spasmodic dysphonia also occurred. Brain MRI and peripheral nerve physiology were normal when performed. The proband developed unilateral upper limb dystonia at age 2 years. It generalized to the trunk and all limbs and caused loss of ambulation. His father and grandfather had the hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotype, with progressive leg weakness and spasticity beginning after age 20 years. Metabolic studies were normal in the proband and his father, including blood lactate and pyruvate, serum amino acids, urine organic acids, and acylcarnitine profiles.

paragraphs.text: Zech et al. (2022) described 3 unrelated patients with ATP5MC3 variants. Patient 8, a previously reported 12-year-old boy, had isolated upper-limb dystonia. Patient 9, a 15-year-old girl, had a history of milestone delay, pyramidal signs, and generalized dystonia with prominent upper-body involvement. Patient 10, a 6-year-old boy, had delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate. Zech et al. (2022) combined their 3 patients with the multigenerational family reported by Neilson et al. (2022). Across these 18 individuals, the ATP5MC3-associated condition included dystonia (12/18), spasticity/pyramidal signs (17/18), and developmental delay/intellectual disability (2/18). Ten individuals had dystonia-predominant syndromes. The authors noted that patients 9 and 10 confirmed spastic symptoms in independent families and added neurodevelopmental comorbidity to the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Gilbert et al. (2009) mapped the disease locus in the Ohio kindred to chromosome 2q24-q31. They used single-point and multipoint linkage analysis with microsatellite markers and SNP array genotyping. The region was flanked by rs1424937 and rs1559510, lay proximal to SPG13, and contained no known hereditary spastic paraplegia or dystonia genes. A secondary analysis looked for candidate regions segregating with the dystonia phenotype and found 2 regions with parametric lod scores above 2.0.

paragraphs.text: Family-1 of Neilson et al. (2022) had a disorder previously mapped to chromosome 2q24-q31. In affected members, the authors used whole-exome sequencing restricted to the linkage region and identified a heterozygous c.318C-G mutation in the ATP5MC3 gene, resulting in an asn106-to-lys (N106K) substitution. Sanger sequencing showed that only affected individuals carried the variant. The variant was absent from gnomAD v2.1.1 and v3.1.1. It affects a highly conserved loop that contacts the F1 subunit, and all in silico tools used predicted it to be damaging. Fibroblasts from 2 affected family members showed reduced complex V activity, cellular ATP, and oxygen consumption. GeneMatcher identified the Family-2 proband, and parent-offspring trio whole-exome sequencing in him found the same heterozygous N106K mutation, which had arisen de novo. The authors stated that this result confirmed the pathogenicity of the variant for dystonia. They also screened 384 patients, 362 with dystonia and 22 with hereditary spastic paraplegia, for variants in ATP5MC1, ATP5MC2, and ATP5MC3 and found no deleterious variants.

paragraphs.text: Zech et al. (2022) performed whole-exome sequencing in a cohort of 1,012 dystonia patients. In a 12-year-old boy with isolated upper-limb dystonia (patient 8), they found a de novo heterozygous N106K mutation in ATP5MC3. In a 15-year-old girl with milestone delay, pyramidal signs, and generalized dystonia (patient 9), they identified a de novo heterozygous pro107-to-ala (P107A) mutation. In a 6-year-old boy with delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate (patient 10), they identified a de novo heterozygous gly79-to-val (G79V) mutation. All 3 variants were absent from gnomAD. Patient fibroblasts showed decreased ATPase activity for N106K and G79V.

paragraphs.text: Neilson et al. (2022) studied affected members of a large multigenerational family (Family-1) with autosomal dominant dystonia and/or spastic paraplegia. Using whole-exome sequencing restricted to the linkage region on chromosome 2q24-q31, they identified a heterozygous c.318C-G transversion in the ATP5MC3 gene, resulting in an asn106-to-lys (N106K) substitution. Sanger sequencing showed that only affected individuals carried the variant. It was absent from gnomAD v2.1.1 and v3.1.1, affects a highly conserved loop that contacts the F1 subunit, and was predicted damaging by all in silico tools used. Fibroblasts from the proband and his affected father showed complex V activity reduced by 20%, cellular ATP reduced by 20 to 32%, and oxygen consumption reduced by 21 to 25%. Neilson et al. (2022) also identified the same mutation, which had arisen de novo, by trio whole-exome sequencing in a boy of European descent with upper limb dystonia (Family-2).

paragraphs.text: Zech et al. (2022) studied a 6-year-old boy (patient 10) with delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate. They identified a de novo heterozygous c.236G-T transversion in the ATP5MC3 gene, resulting in a gly79-to-val (G79V) substitution. The variant was absent from gnomAD. Patient fibroblasts showed deficient ATPase activity and a moderate decrease in assembled ATPase on BN-PAGE. The ATPase enzyme deficit was significantly greater than that seen with the N106K mutation. Modeling placed gly79 at an interhelical contact site, where the substitution might interfere with c-ring integrity.
